title: [WT-11] Wrappers: unlanded route and conflict resume inside the task worktree
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §2.5 and §2.6.

Objective: a landing that cannot reach the target parks its bytes on a rescue ref and sends the task back through the daemon (WT-03). That covers a true conflict, lost contention, a failed gate, a diverged target and a lease timeout. The next worker resolves the conflict inside W. Nothing is ever resolved automatically or silently overwritten.

Deliverable, in scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 as twins:
- On each unlanded cause:
  - record_commit failed with its code (MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_CONFLICT, MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_REF_CONTENTION, MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE, MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED; MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_LAND_LEASE maps to reason contention);
  - a rescue ref refs/moe/rescue/<taskId>/<ts> at T (reason conflict|contention|gate|diverged);
  - `finalize_attempt { outcome:'unlanded', landedRevision:null, unlandedReason, conflictPaths, rescueRef }` (WT-03, task-9a39bf6a2c4444b4b0799cd16dc2a9f1).
- The next worker pre-flight with task.landingRetry set runs `git -C W -c core.hooksPath=<empty dir> merge --no-commit --no-ff refs/heads/<target>` and starts the prompt with `LANDING-CONFLICT: <paths>` or `LANDING-RETRY: <reason>`. The prompt tells the worker to edit files only, re-run verification and call complete_task.
- Marker check before a completion's L2 when MERGE_HEAD is set: lines starting '<<<<<<< ' or '>>>>>>> ', or equal to '=======', in landingRetry.paths plus `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` give MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT and the unlanded route again. A clean scan commits with MERGE_HEAD as the second parent, then `git -C W merge --quit`.
- A checkpoint during a pending merge commits with one parent and keeps MERGE_HEAD.
- Teardown: a signal before L9 abandons the landing; during L9-L12 it is deferred until L12 returns. A REVIEW task whose attempt is still finalizing re-runs L4-L12 at the next pre-flight, or replays the receipt journal.
- Cases in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and postflight.ps1. Depends on WT-10 (task-5c2e6cdf2494412ca0c2bc40e26d9da3) and WT-03.

NOT in scope: daemon routing (WT-03); board snapshot (WT-12); removal (WT-14); docs (WT-17/WT-18).

Verification: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh (and on a Windows seat: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell)
definitionOfDone: postflight case (both harnesses): a same-line conflict leaves main unchanged, creates refs/moe/rescue/<taskId>/<ts> at T, and the fake proxy receives finalize_attempt outcome 'unlanded' with reason 'conflict' and the conflicting path.

postflight case: the next session with landingRetry set gets markers in W and MERGE_HEAD, and its prompt starts with 'LANDING-CONFLICT:'; a contention or gate retry merges cleanly and gets 'LANDING-RETRY:'.

postflight case: a completion with markers still present prints MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT and lands nothing; after the markers are removed it lands C on main and the task-branch commit has MERGE_HEAD as its second parent; MERGE_HEAD is gone afterwards.
postflight case: a checkpoint during the pending merge has exactly one parent and MERGE_HEAD survives it.
bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh passes unchanged; existing postflight cases pass; both wrappers carry the same MOE_WORKTREE_/MOE_LAND_/MOE_CONTROL_/MOE_BOARD_ codes.
The verification command exits 0; postflight.ps1 passes on a Windows seat.

implementationPlan.description: 1. Pin the unlanded contract in the existing fixture and twin tests first. Goal: confirmed-unpublished failures safely return to a worker; unknown/published outcomes do not. Architecture: wrapper preserves T and reports unlanded to WT-03; subsequent claim merges the authoritative target into W; completed plan steps stay completed. Tech: Git, Bash/Python, PS5.1 and the existing Node fake proxy. Read the landed WT-03/WT-10 contracts plus task comments and revised design §2.5/2.6; use their actual helper names. Extend only the shared postflight-fake-proxy.js finalizeReply/get_context fixture: accept unlanded only for a worktree finalizing attempt, require landedRevision:null, a reason in conflict|contention|gate|diverged|remote, same-task rescueRef, optional 40-hex/null targetTip, and normalized bounded conflictPaths. Assert failed record_commit precedes it and no pushed:true/landed row for that failure. Return/store fixture landingRetry as WT-03 does; expose it conditionally in context; duplicate finalize must not increment the retry count twice. Keep all old outcomes and strict assertions unchanged. Reuse landed workspace/claim knobs rather than duplicate the proxy. In both harnesses add table-driven failure rows for conflict, contention, gate, diverged, lease timeout -> contention, fetch failure/proven-absent push -> remote; assert exact payload, target unchanged, rescue resolves to T and no landed finalize. Include unknown-push negative row: no finalize of ANY outcome. Do not modify held-out worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} or daemon files.
implementationPlan.note:
I pinned the unlanded contract first.

- **Fake proxy** (`postflight-fake-proxy.js`):
  - finalize_attempt now accepts 'unlanded' through `unlandedCheck`, which mirrors finalizeAttempt.ts validateUnlanded. It requires a worktree attempt, landedRevision null, one of the five reasons, a rescue ref of this task, a 40-hex or null targetTip, and at most 500 distinct relative paths. Every completion row of the session must be failed, coded and pushed:false.
  - An unlanded close of a finalizing attempt stores landing-retry.json with count+1. A closed replay leaves the count alone. landed and nothing-to-commit clear it.
  - get_context serves the stored value as task.landingRetry.
- **Scope growth:** the new cases live in the shared scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs instead of postflight.sh/.ps1. Both harnesses already run it (postflight.sh:1257, postflight.ps1:1238), so the twin tests have one source. The held-out worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} and the daemon files are untouched.
- **New cases:**
  - **'wt-unlanded'** is table-driven:
    - conflict;
    - contention via WT_GIT_FAIL '-m', which fails only the landing CAS, plus finalize-loss-once to prove a replayed finalize counts once;
    - gate;
    - lease timeout → contention, tip null;
    - diverged;
    - fetch failure → remote, tip null. Its resume fetch failing stops with MOE_WORKTREE_RESUME_FAILED and launches no CLI;
    - [remote rejected] → remote. Its resume merges origin's peer-pushed tip, never the local main.

    Each row is then resumed and checked for its prompt prefix, MERGE_HEAD and an unchanged main. The case also covers resolved-to-T (still [T,B] on T's tree) and an unknown push that finalizes nothing.
  - **'wt-resume'** is the DoD 2-4 chain: markers + MERGE_HEAD + 'LANDING-CONFLICT: src/a.txt'; a one-parent checkpoint that keeps MERGE_HEAD and the 3 unmerged stages; a completion with markers that prints MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT and lands nothing; then the resolved landing, with the L2 commit's second parent = B, MERGE_HEAD gone and the retry cleared.
  - **'marker-scan'** unit-tests the wrapper's own scanner: each marker shape, CRLF, a path out of W, a resolved deletion and look-alikes.
  - **wt-replay-remote run 4:** a finalizing journaled attempt is routed unlanded 'remote'.
- **RED** on the scratch snapshot /tmp/wt11-red: all 4 cases fail for the missing feature, not for harness errors. For example, conflict gets a legacy row with pushed undefined and reason=commit-failed, and marker-scan reports "no function wt_marker_scan".
- Peer sessions' dirty .moe/roles, .moe/skills and .moe/tasks paths and scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js predate this session's edits on other lines. They are not reverted or staged by me beyond the listed files.

implementationPlan.description: 2. Route only proven-unpublished failures through one worktree unlanded result. Map MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_CONFLICT and MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT to conflict; MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_REF_CONTENTION/MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_LAND_LEASE to contention; MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE (including gate integrity failures) to gate; MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED to diverged; MOE_LAND_FETCH_FAILED and a reconciled absent MOE_PUSH_FAILED to remote. Reuse predecessor publication-state tracking: confirmed C or an unknown push must bypass this route even if a later sync/RPC fails. Preserve T by the existing rescue-from-commit primitive at refs/moe/rescue/<taskId>/<timestamp>, with mapped reason, and confirm it resolves to T; marker rejection before L2 must also leave all working bytes untouched. Send failed completion record_commit with the code and pushed:false, then finalize_attempt with `{outcome:'unlanded',landedRevision:null,unlandedReason,conflictPaths,rescueRef,targetTip:B_or_null}` plus pinned identity/runner fields. Extend finalize_attempt_rpc/Send-MoeFinalize and final postflight dispatch so ordinary teardown cannot issue a second legacy finalize. Error handling: rescue creation failure or failed ledger/finalize acknowledgement retains bytes, attempt hold and retry data, stops new-task claiming, and retries the same action rather than reporting successful handback. Reuse existing bounded RPC retries and idempotent finalization; do not edit daemon-owned task state or reopen plan steps. Unknown push remains WT-09's journal/reconciliation-only path.
implementationPlan.note: Unlanded route in both wrappers. sh: unlanded_reason (code->reason map), unlanded_park (rescue ref at T unless L2's own contention ref exists, then record_commit failed/code/pushed:false), take_unlanded_route (signals deferred, land lease released first, MOE_UNLANDED_REASON/TIP=LAND_B, finalize_postflight -> finalize_args emits outcome unlanded {landedRevision:null, unlandedReason, conflictPaths (normalized, deduped, <=500, from merge.z), rescueRef, targetTip B|null}); a failed rescue/row finalizes nothing, memoizes MOE_FINALIZE_RC=1 so the seat stops, bytes stay on the task branch. replay_unlanded: a still-finalizing journal whose landing can never apply (receipt_replay rc 1) is parked unlanded/remote instead of dropped (replaces WT-09's drop per comment c2d608e0); a failed route keeps the journal. LAND_WT_REASON removed. ps1 twins: Get-MoeUnlandedFields, Send-MoeFinalize -Extra, Complete-MoePostflight unlanded outcome, Get-MoeJournalAttempt, Invoke-MoeReplayUnlanded, Get-MoeUnlandedReason, Invoke-MoeUnlandedRoute; Sync-MoeLandTarget sets $L.B in both modes (even diverged). MOE_PUSH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and refused outcomes never route. Evidence: sh snapshot MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=wt-replay-remote ok; wt-unlanded conflict row passes every routed assertion (main unchanged, row failed+code+pushed false, finalize unlanded/conflict/['src/a.txt']/tip/null rescue=T, retry count 1) and stops only at the resume prompt (step-3). ps1 (Windows powershell engine via node.exe) wt-replay-remote ok.

implementationPlan.description: 3. Resume a landingRetry in W without overwriting existing resolution work. After WT-04's .moe guard and owner checks, before general dirty recovery or CLI launch, consume task.landingRetry from served context. Obtain the authoritative §1.2 base through the landed target-sync helper: local target in local mode; fetched refs/remotes/origin/<target> in remote mode, never local fallback. Preserve unrelated W dirt with the existing one-parent checkpoint only when no merge is already pending. With no MERGE_HEAD, run `git -C W -c core.hooksPath=<owned empty dir> merge --no-commit --no-ff <base>`. Exit 1 plus actual unmerged paths is an expected conflict; operational errors/failed fetch launch no CLI, leave bytes untouched and report a retryable failure, never reset/clean/abort. If MERGE_HEAD already exists, validate it as a commit and reuse the pending merge and current edits as-is instead of starting a second merge or repeating recovery. Prefix the worker's actual prompt/context with `LANDING-CONFLICT: <paths>` when conflicts are pending, otherwise `LANDING-RETRY: <reason>` (including remote and already-up-to-date cases). Safely render bounded relative paths without shell interpolation; tell the worker to edit files only, remove markers, run the existing plan verification and call complete_task directly, not run Git or re-open completed steps. Tests in both harnesses: same-line conflict yields markers+MERGE_HEAD+prefix; clean contention/gate/remote retry yields retry prefix; remote uses fetched tracking tip rather than stale local; a second resume preserves partial edits and the original merge metadata; fetch/merge operational failure preserves work and does not launch.
implementationPlan.note: Resume of a landingRetry in W. sh worktree_resume (already in checkpoint e1881619) + new ps1 twin Invoke-MoeWorktreeResume, called from worktree_preflight / Invoke-MoeWorktreePreflight right after the recovery checkpoint (ps1 gains a [ref]$Context param at its one call site). Reads task.landingRetry (5 reasons, ≤500 paths kept for step 4's marker scan as MOE_WT_RETRY(_PATHS) / $script:MoeWtRetry(Paths)); reuses an existing MERGE_HEAD (verified to be a commit); else base = refs/heads/<target> without a remote, or refs/remotes/origin/<target> fetched now (3 tries, no local fallback); `git -C W -c core.hooksPath=<owned empty temp dir> merge --no-commit --no-ff <base>`; rc0 or rc1-with-unmerged is ok, anything else → MOE_WORKTREE_RESUME_FAILED (report_blocked, exit 1, no reset/clean/abort so W keeps its bytes). The prompt/context starts `LANDING-CONFLICT: <unmerged paths, ≤20, +N more>` or `LANDING-RETRY: <reason>` plus one instruction line (edit files only, re-run verification, complete_task); identical text in both wrappers. Test fix: the resume launches in wt-unlanded/wt-resume now pass {type:'claude'} (cliShim forwards no argv, so WT_CLI_RECORD saw no prompt). Evidence (scratch snapshots, MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=wt-unlanded,wt-resume): sh and ps1 (Windows PowerShell 5.1) both pass every resume assertion for all 7 rows (conflict→'LANDING-CONFLICT: src/a.txt' + MERGE_HEAD=main tip + main unchanged; contention/gate/lease/diverged→'LANDING-RETRY: …' with no MERGE_HEAD; fetch→refused MOE_WORKTREE_RESUME_FAILED with W bytes kept; rejected→'LANDING-RETRY: remote' with MERGE_HEAD = origin's peer commit, not the stale local main); wt-resume run 2 prompt/MERGE_HEAD/markers/one-parent checkpoint pass. Remaining failures are exactly step-4 items: 'resolved to T' (two-parent L2 + merge --quit) and the 3 unmerged stages (checkpoint must not reset the real index under MERGE_HEAD). Tests live in the shared postflight-worktree.cjs (both harnesses). No peer dirty paths touched; held-out worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} and daemon files untouched.

implementationPlan.description: 4. Make L2 aware of pending merges and marker safety. When a completion has MERGE_HEAD, collect the deduplicated union of landingRetry.paths and `git -C W diff --name-only -z --diff-filter=U`; validate paths are W-relative and contained, do not follow outside symlinks. Read regular-file bytes linewise, treating CRLF as line endings, and reject lines beginning `<<<<<<< ` or `>>>>>>> `, or exactly `=======`. Missing paths can represent resolved deletion; other unreadable/unsafe paths are refusal, never a clean scan. Any hit emits MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT, leaves W/real index/MERGE_HEAD untouched and takes step 2's conflict route. After a clean scan, use the private temp index to stage the resolution, then `commit-tree <resolved-tree> -p T -p <saved MERGE_HEAD>` and the existing task-branch CAS; this commit is required even if the resolved tree equals T. Refresh the real index without discarding W changes and run `git -C W merge --quit` ONLY after successful CAS. On failure preserve pending metadata and prevent publication until recoverable. A checkpoint during MERGE_HEAD uses only parent T and does not reset/read-tree the REAL index or call merge --quit: preserve its unmerged stages and MERGE_HEAD, while using the temp index for the checkpoint. This avoids reset -q clearing the merge and avoids losing new conflict names after a checkpoint. Tests: each marker shape and CRLF refuses with main unchanged; marker-free merge lands C and a task commit whose second parent is the saved MERGE_HEAD; resolved-to-T still records merge ancestry; deletion resolution; interrupted checkpoint has exactly one parent with MERGE_HEAD and unmerged paths surviving; later completion still scans all those paths. Do not silently choose ours/theirs.
implementationPlan.note: Step 4 done in both wrappers. A completion's L2 first runs a marker scan (sh wt_merge_check + wt_marker_scan, ps1 Find-MoeConflictMarkers + Get-MoeUnmergedPaths) over landingRetry.paths plus W's unmerged paths whenever MERGE_HEAD is present or a landingRetry is set. A hit (a '<<<<<<< '/'>>>>>>> ' prefix or an exact '=======' line; a path that resolves outside W, a link, a directory or an unreadable file also counts as a hit, the same in both wrappers) gives MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT, commits nothing, leaves W, its index and MERGE_HEAD alone, and takes step 2's conflict route with those paths as conflictPaths. The completion now carries L2's own message forward instead of 'the task-branch commit failed'. After a clean scan, commit-tree -p T -p MERGE_HEAD runs even when the tree equals T. The real index is refreshed, and `git merge --quit` runs only after the CAS succeeds. A checkpoint during a merge (LAND_KEEP_INDEX / $M.KeepIndex) has a single parent, skips the real-index refresh and keeps MERGE_HEAD and the unmerged stages. Addition beyond the plan text: the merge seed (wt_merge_seed / Get-MoeMergeSeed). With MERGE_HEAD as the second parent, landing's merge-base becomes MH and T'^{tree} lands verbatim. If the temp index were seeded from T, every DENY path B changed but the task never stages (.gemini/**, the sparse .moe/) would be reverted on main. The seed is git's merge of T and MH, taking T's side on conflicted paths. If staging drops any path of a pending merge, the result is MOE_COMMIT_FAILED (a merge lands whole or not at all). Test: the wt-resume B now also changes .gemini/g.md, and run 4 asserts main keeps 'main g'. In a mutation run (seed=T) it went RED with "path '.gemini/g.md' does not exist in C"; with the real code it is GREEN. Harness fix: resume launches use {type:'claude'}, because cliShim drops argv and only typeShim forwards the prompt to WT_CLI_RECORD. Evidence: MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=marker-scan,wt-resume,wt-unlanded passes on bash (3 ok, 0 failed) and on Windows PowerShell 5.1 via node.exe (3 ok, 0 failed), both from snapshots outside the checkout. The ps1 parses clean with the PS Parser API and keeps its BOM and LF line endings.

implementationPlan.description: 5. Complete worktree teardown and finalizing-attempt recovery. Reuse WT-08/09's publication journal/state and WT-10's lease cleanup. Before L9, cancellation abandons publication and preserves task bytes/checkpoint/rescue without a main move. During L9-L12, defer handled cancellation until publication is classified and its ledger/finalize sequence finishes; release any lease in finally on all paths. Bash traps set a pending-stop flag during the narrow critical window and run the normal stop afterwards. PowerShell must use a native event handler/owned-process mechanism that is safe on 5.1 and 7, never a Console.CancelKeyPress PowerShell scriptblock (verified source warning); preserve existing handler/console settings and detach only this invocation's handler after the window. A forced process death is not claimed to be deferrable: recover from the durable journal. On next pre-flight, a REVIEW task with the pinned finalizing attempt first replays/reconciles its journal; confirmed publication owes only sync/ledger/finalize, proven absence reruns L4-L12 in W under the owner guard, unknown remote outcome stays finalizing with no finalize/no new CLI. Never apply a second landing to an already-contained C or let generic teardown turn unknown into failed/unlanded. Use the existing owned-console/signal test supervisor and deterministic Git/RPC barriers in both harnesses: interrupt before publish, after publish before sync, during ledger/finalize, hard death then replay, and unknown push then restart. Assert target/rescue/attempt truth, exactly one completion, no premature unlanded, lease released and no leaked child process; no sleep-only race tests.
implementationPlan.note:
Teardown and finalizing-attempt recovery are in both wrappers, with twin tests.

**Deferral window**
- sh: wt_defer_signals / wt_release_signals. A trap sets MOE_WT_SIGNALED from the CAS until the ledger row and finalize are done. After that it prints "Agent stopped." and the EXIT trap runs as usual.
- ps1: Set-MoeCtrlCDeferred is an Add-Type native SetConsoleCtrlHandler delegate. It records the hit and swallows the event. On/Off are idempotent and Off detaches only this handler. There is no CancelKeyPress scriptblock.
- Before the CAS, an interrupt abandons the landing: main unmoved, no journal, T keeps the bytes, finalize 'failed', never unlanded. The lease is released in the finally/EXIT path on all paths.

**Replay**
- Journaled C absent from the target while the pinned attempt is still finalizing (proven absence) → replay_unlanded / Invoke-MoeReplayUnlanded route it unlanded 'contention' (MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_REF_CONTENTION). T is rescued and B is the targetTip.
- The replay never re-lands. The next worker re-runs L4-L12 in W under the owner guard through the landingRetry resume. This follows the one-route-helper rule (comments c2d608e0, 0a216f7e, §2.6).
- Confirmed publication sends the row and finalize landed. The sync is left to the next pre-flight's recorded-C sync.
- Unknown remote outcome keeps the journal and finalizes nothing.

**Defect found by the full ps1 run, fixed**
- The ps1 route sent no failed row when the rescue ref failed; sh's unlanded_park always sends it.
- This made WT-08's wt-exhausted and wt-gate-exhausted fail on ps1.
- Fixed in Invoke-MoeUnlandedRoute and Invoke-MoeReplayUnlanded: the row is now always sent, and the route needs both the row and the ref.

**Harness**
Same scope growth as step-1: the shared postflight-worktree.cjs, which postflight.sh and postflight.ps1 both run.
- launch() gains opts.keep, opts.ready and opts.kill, plus a sh process-group leak check.
- New consoleSupervisor: an owned hidden console, a real GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent, and a leaked-child check via Win32_Process.
- New cases:
  - wt-teardown: pre / sync / ledger.
  - wt-crash: cas / sync, each a hard kill and then a same-seat restart replay.
  - wt-replay-remote: an unknown-outcome restart that keeps the journal, sends no finalize, launches no CLI and leaves the attempt finalizing.
- Fake proxy: FAKE_HOLD_DRAIN=1, opt-in, so a held call survives Ctrl+C the way moe-proxy drains.

- ps1 5.1: full suite 45 ok + 2 failed; after the fix, wt-fails, wt-gate, wt-unlanded, wt-replay-remote and wt-crash re-run 5/5 ok.
- pwsh 7: wt-teardown and wt-crash ok.
- RED checks:
  - sh, deferral made a no-op → teardown 'sync' fails.
  - sh, replay finalizing branch off → crash 'cas' fails.
  - ps1, deferral made a no-op → teardown 'sync' fails.

Peer dirty paths (.moe/roles, .moe/skills, other task json, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, moe-jetbrains, moe-vscode, local-runner-bundle test, bundle-manifest) were left untouched.

implementationPlan.description: 7. Final adversarial self-review and handoff. Load adversarial-self-review once, then inspect this task's diff for: unknown versus absent remote outcome; duplicate/lost finalize replies; rescue creation failure; stale assignee or identity; concurrent target advance; pending merge checkpoint clearing metadata; unmerged path loss; marker-free equal-tree merge; path traversal/symlink reads/CRLF; cancellation on either side of publication; finalizing replay that accidentally re-gates/relands a published C; and cleanup leaking a lease/child. Map every DoD to twin assertions, with held-out tests untouched. Confirm shared mode and daemon-only .moe writing are preserved. Keep this ≤400 net non-board lines by reusing landed helpers/fixtures; no broad refactor, docs, board snapshot or worktree removal. Fix any defects in the five declared files and rerun the same gate if bytes change. Worker uses complete_task with fresh evidence and records a handoff; wrapper owns commits. Whole-epic adversarial review/docs remain later tasks.
implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review of `git diff c46c4a8c` over the four changed files (skill loaded once this session). One defect was found and fixed in-step, and the gate was re-run on the final bytes (see the step-6 note). The defect: the marker scan had linked-parent, unparseable-name and FIFO holes. Bytes unchanged since the gates (sha256 -c OK).

Risk list:
- Unknown vs absent remote outcome: an unsettled push (reconcile rc=2) is MOE_PUSH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN: journal kept, no finalize, never routed (wtUnlanded 'unknown'). A hook rejection is MOE_PUSH_FAILED and routes 'remote' (wtUnlanded 'rejected'). A non-ff rejection or origin moved without C triggers the next round, and contention after the last one. In replay, rc=2 keeps the journal with no finalize (wt-replay-remote-down); rc=1 on a still-finalizing attempt routes unlanded 'remote'.
- Duplicate/lost finalize: wtUnlanded 'contention' runs with finalize-loss-once and the retry counts once. Theoretical: a lost replay finalize keeps the journal, so the next replay re-parks (a second rescue ref and failed row) before finalizing again.
- Rescue failure: the row still goes, nothing finalizes and the seat stops (wt-fails/wt-gate exhausted, both twins).
- Stale identity: replay checks the journal's pinned attempt via moe_pinned_attempt_phase and skips a live foreign marker. The row's sessionId is the replaying session, which made the rescue ref.
- Concurrent target advance: one CAS per round, then contention.
- Pending-merge checkpoint: one parent, index kept, no merge --quit (wtResume run 2).
- Unmerged path loss: the scan covers retry paths plus unmerged paths. W's bytes are staged onto merge-tree's seed with T's side on conflicted paths (wtResume run 4: resolved, B's m.txt, partial p.txt, B's DENY .gemini/g.md kept).
- Equal-tree merge: forced [T,B] commit (wtUnlanded 'resolved to T').
- Traversal/symlink/CRLF: markerScan.
- Cancellation on either side of publication: wtTeardown pre/sync/ledger (real Ctrl+C on ps1).
- Replay never re-gates or relands: wtCrash sync (no CLI, main parents [B]).
- Lease/child leaks: lease released before deregister, holders []; sh process-group check; ps1 console supervisor.

DoD mapping:
1. wtUnlanded 'conflict'.
2. wtUnlanded resume prompts plus wtResume run 2.
3. wtResume runs 3 and 4.
4. wtResume run 2.
5. worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} 18/18 and unchanged vs 8ad04de7 and HEAD; postflight scenarios A..Z pass; codes case plus identical 25-token sets.
6. Gate rc=0 and postflight.ps1 exit 0 on Windows.

Shared mode is unchanged: finalize_args emits the same payload for non-unlanded outcomes, and the L2 knobs are worktree-local. The wrappers write no .moe state; only the fake proxy stands in for the daemon.

The daemon contract WT-11 builds against, from WT-03's plan (task-9a39bf6a):
- finalize_attempt { outcome:'unlanded', landedRevision: null (a non-null value is refused), unlandedReason: conflict|contention|gate|diverged|remote, conflictPaths: string[] (optional; normalized, deduped, capped at 500, invalid entries dropped), rescueRef: 'refs/moe/rescue/<taskId>/<ts>' (required, must name this task), targetTip: B as 40 hex (optional, else null) }.
- It is refused with INVALID_INPUT unless the attempt is workspaceMode 'worktree' and finalizing. Those four fields are ignored on every other outcome.
- The response adds taskStatus and landingRetry.
- task.landingRetry {reason, paths, rescueRef, targetTip, count, at} is readable in get_context's task (absent when unset). 'landed' and 'nothing-to-commit' clear it.
- Routing: REVIEW to WORKING, unassigned. REVIEW to BLOCKED (blockedFromStatus WORKING) for 'diverged', or from the 3rd consecutive unlanded. A row not in REVIEW keeps its status.
- Plan steps stay COMPLETED, so the resumed worker can call complete_task directly.

comments.author: qa-952969be
comments.content:
QA note from the WT-S round-2 review (qa-952969be). Contract correction for docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §2.2 L2 versus §2.5.

The problem:
- L2 ends with `git -C W reset -q`.
- A mixed `git reset` with no pathspec deletes MERGE_HEAD and drops the unmerged index entries. I reproduced this on git 2.43 in a scratch repo: a `merge --no-commit` conflict, then `reset -q`, and MERGE_HEAD is gone.
- So a checkpoint taken during a pending merge cannot "leave MERGE_HEAD in place" as §2.5 says. The same goes for §3.3's recovery checkpoint.
- The next completion then skips the marker check, which only runs when MERGE_HEAD is set, and commits with one parent.
- L5 usually catches the conflict again, because the old merge base is kept. But a resume that spans sessions then loops or nests markers. If the target's side of the conflict has since been reverted, markers can merge cleanly.

Fix it in this slice:
- While MERGE_HEAD is set, L2 must not reset, or must restore MERGE_HEAD and the unmerged entries.
- Run the marker scan whenever task.landingRetry is set, not only when MERGE_HEAD is.
- Add a case: a checkpoint during a merge keeps MERGE_HEAD, and the completion still refuses leftover markers.
